column9: COVID-era emergency rollout; April 1-3 2020 drive-up distribution of ~5,600 Chromebooks for gr3-12; superintendent called it 'unprecedented'; federal COVID relief funds used to become a 1:1 district; no pre-2020 1:1 program documented

COVID-era 2020: 4,000+ Chromebooks + 1,400 Wi-Fi hotspots distributed via distance learning program; additional 2,000 Chromebooks + accessories over summer 2020 for 2020-21 SY; no pre-2020 district-wide 1:1 documented

PreK-Grade 1 iPad; Grades 2-12 Chromebook; Google Apps for Education; COVID-era distribution confirmed (sign-up required, social distancing protocols); exact launch year undocumented; upper bound 2020
Chromebooks confirmed in use at middle schools; district-wide 1:1 status and launch year not found; upper bound from COVID-era evidence

Oct 1 2018 rollout; ~6,000 Dell 5190 2-in-1 Chromebooks to MS + HS students; $2.75M funded via Education SPLOST; carrying case + charger included; Google Suite + classroom filtering; first press release dated Sep 27 2018

ESSER-funded 1:1 Chromebook rollout for all PK-12 students; ESSER I ($2.6M) + ESSER II ($11.1M) + ESSER III ($24.9M) financed technology; K-2 touchscreen Chromebooks; 3-12 standard Chromebooks; article dated March 2022 describes ongoing implementation

COVID-era April 2020 full 1:1 take-home rollout; district had Chromebooks since 2014 for CAASPP testing (~2,100 devices) but not take-home 1:1; April 2020 cleaning + reconfiguring devices + new hotspots for 11K+ students; now all gr1-12 take home daily
COVID-era: district web page for 'Student laptop/Chromebook distribution' under COVID-19 Updates; Chromebook languages page exists; no pre-2020 1:1 launch date documented; upper bound 2020

column9: Bonneville was among 32 Idaho districts selected for state 1:1 HS laptop program (Students Come First); HS laptops from state began fall 2013; district expanded to full K-12 1:1 Chromebook program; Voluntary Chromebook Protection Plan and RUA documents on district site

BYOD program documented (board policy); district uses Chromebooks and iPads (mentioned in 2025 technology needs); no explicit 1:1 launch date found; upper bound from COVID-era technology distribution; 2026 bond includes $9.1M for device replacement

column9: 2011: STEM Academy HS magnet launched with 1:1 laptop per student; 2013: Ivy Academy blended learning at conventional HS; district-wide 1:1 initiative formalized; current K-8 two-in-one Chromebook + 9-12 Windows two-in-one for home+school

April 2020 COVID-era: principals distributed ~1,700 Chromebooks from dismantled testing carts; ordered 3,500 more (CARES Act funded) Aug 2020 for remote learning; 10,000+ total devices managed; pre-COVID had carts/labs but not 1:1 take-home

COVID-era Spring 2020: HP 11 Chromebooks distributed to students for distance learning; district created guides and tutorials; Wi-Fi hotspots (up to 10 devices) deployed; ESSER + CA state funds used; no pre-2020 1:1 found

Board approved 'Waukesha One' iPad 1:1 program May 2013; pilot at 4 schools (North Blair Bethesda Hillcrest) funded ~$349K Apr 2015; full K-12 iPad rollout by Sep 2016; ~$3M/yr; teachers got MacBook Air + iPad; students got iPad; 26 schools total

iConnect@Warren initiative; 1:1 Chromebook for every gr1-12 student + iPad for K; funded partly by $28.5M Race to the Top grant (won 2012); program rolled out after 2012 grant; upper bound 2014 (earliest firm evidence)

1:1 Chromebook gr3-12 confirmed; 2017 bond ($156M) included technology upgrades; 2022 bond also included tech; no specific launch date found for 1:1 program; upper bound 2020 (COVID-era rollout confirmed on district site)

District-issued Chromebooks for all students; middle school take-home policy changed (no longer going home at MS); Feb 2025: $700K contract to upgrade inventory; no specific 1:1 launch year documented; upper bound 2020

1:M initiative launched 2014-15 SY after years of research and device testing; K-2 iPad; gr3-8 Chromebook; gr9-12 MacBook Air; $25/yr family fee; devices go home; district researched 1:1 options for several years before launch

column7: Grades 2-12 class sets; not confirmed full 1:1 take-home pre-2020
column9: Measure A bond (passed Nov 2014) funded class sets of Chromebooks for gr2-12 in core subjects plus iPads/Chromebooks for TK-1; COVID ESSER funds ($179K+$586K+) for devices; described as classroom class sets not 1:1 take-home pre-COVID; upper bound 2020

1:1 Chromebook program with home-learning support; COVID-era 2020 board voted to extend closure Apr 3 2020; district has Home Learning resource page + troubleshooting guides; no specific pre-2020 1:1 launch date found; upper bound 2020

1:1 district: iPads + MacBooks issued to all students for take-home use; JAMF Pro device management; device insurance program; no specific launch year found; $120M bond passed April 2023 (no-tax-increase); upper bound 2020

1:1 Technology Program established fall 2020; all gr3-12 issued Chromebook; existing supply of Chromebooks used to reduce startup cost; students use division-issued device or approved personal device; device refresh cycle tracks same device for multiple years

Junior High 1:1 Chromebook take-home program confirmed; K-8 district in Ontario San Bernardino County; Chromebooks charged and brought to school daily; no specific launch year documented; upper bound 2020

column9: Nov 2013: voters approved $45M bond; March 2014: board authorized $25M first series; 1:1 Chromebook program launched (gr5 and gr9 get new device to keep for 4 years then pass down); bond projects largely complete by fall 2015; $75/student/yr technology fee from 2022-23
